controls.label: Query matrix Q
controls.help: Editing Q changes the raw query-key dot products in the Similarity scores S, which changes the Attention weights A, the Peak weight of query 1 and the Attention output O.

controls.label: Key matrix K
controls.help: Editing K changes the raw query-key dot products in the Similarity scores S, which changes the Attention weights A, the Row sums of A check and the Attention output O.

controls.label: Value matrix V
controls.help: Editing V leaves the Similarity scores S and Attention weights A unchanged but directly changes the Attention output O because O is a weighted average of the rows of V.

controls.label: Key dimension d_k
controls.help: Increasing d_k enlarges the divisor sqrt(d_k) when scaling is on, so the Similarity scores S shrink, the Attention weights A flatten, the Peak weight of query 1 falls and O moves toward a simple average of the value vectors. When scaling is off, d_k has no effect.

controls.label: Apply 1/sqrt(d_k) scaling
controls.help: Turning scaling off removes the divisor, so the Similarity scores S equal the raw dot products, the Attention weights A become sharper and the Peak weight of query 1 rises.

explorations.title: Equal keys give uniform attention
explorations.instruction: Predict: will the two attention weights in each row stay equal, and what fraction will each be? Then apply the preset, which sets the key matrix K so both keys are identical.
explorations.observe: Both rows of the Attention weights A become 0.5 and 0.5, the Row sums of A read 1 and 1, and the Peak weight of query 1 reads 0.5. The Attention output O becomes the average of the two value vectors.
explorations.why: Identical keys make both query-key dot products equal, so the Similarity scores S are equal within each row and the row-wise softmax assigns exactly half the weight to each key.

explorations.title: Dominant score without scaling
explorations.instruction: Predict: with scaling off and one large dot product, how close to one can the larger attention weight get? Then apply the preset, which sets scaling off and a dominant score in the first query row.
explorations.observe: The first row of the Attention weights A becomes about 0.9975 and 0.0025, the Peak weight of query 1 reads about 0.9975, the Row sums of A still read 1 and 1, and the Attention output O is almost equal to the first value vector.
explorations.why: Without the 1/sqrt(d_k) divisor the raw first-row scores are 6 and 0, so the softmax saturates and puts almost all weight on the first key; the Row sums of A remain 1 because softmax always normalizes each row.
